_comment_family: The heavier of the two cuts fitness-story is set in, and the one its
picked words are drawn in. See hanken-grotesk-italic.json, which is
the block's face and carries the note on what this typeface used to
be called.
These two files do not share name ID 1 — this one says 'Hanken
Grotesk SemiBold' and the Italic says 'Hanken Grotesk' — so unlike
the two Telegraf packs they are not strictly forced to declare a full
name. They do anyway, and for a reason that outlives that detail: ID
1 here still names a WEIGHT and not a cut, so 'Hanken Grotesk
SemiBold' is a name the upright SemiBold answers to as well, and this
channel's block already leans. A picked word that came back upright
would not read as a different word, it would read as a mistake.
The typographic family (name ID 16) is 'Hanken Grotesk' on both
files, which is the level at which they really are one family. That
is exactly why neither pack may be declared at it.
Weight 600, which is what the file's OS/2 table says and what the cut
is. Asking for 700 invites a browser to synthesise the difference on
top of a face that already has most of it.
Registered at style normal, the same way rift and the Italic beside
it are. The slant is drawn into the letterforms; declaring the face
italic as well would leave the canvas — which asks for normal —
either missing it or being handed a synthetic oblique of something
else. Normal means 'this file, as drawn'.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
The first is the PostScript name and is also what the installer
registers the face under; the second is the Windows full name. Both
name this one cut rather than a weight or a family, so a machine
answering to either is answering with this file — which is exactly
what the fallback route is for. Neither 'Hanken Grotesk' nor 'Hanken
Grotesk SemiBold' is listed: the first is the Italic's, and the
second would let the upright SemiBold answer.
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice — a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken, not merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before it is ever
drawn. Segoe UI Semibold is named first because it is the nearest
weight every Windows this app runs on is certain to have, and because
falling through to plain Segoe UI would land a picked word at the
same weight as the block around it — which is the one failure that
would look like nothing had gone wrong at all.
stack: 'Hanken Grotesk SemiBold Italic', 'Segoe UI Semibold', 'Segoe UI', Arial, sans-serif
